text: Today, the Coca-Cola system sells more than thirty-three billion cases of drinks a year, in over two hundred countries and territories. In 2024, the company's revenue was about forty-seven billion dollars.
And it still works a lot like Candler's deal. The company mostly makes the concentrate and builds the brand. Independent bottling partners turn it into drinks and get them to stores.

Look back at the whole story, and the recipe was never the whole secret. Free samples got people to try it. A one-dollar deal put it in every town. A bottle made it hard to fake. A war carried it around the world. And when the company tried to change it, its own customers wouldn't let it.
John Pemberton sold about nine glasses a day. He thought he'd made a medicine. What he actually started was a habit... repeated two point two billion times a day.
